title: fix(plugin-auth)!: with SSO domain verification on, an SSO sign-in links to an existing account, or changes its email address, only at a domain the provider has proven
body:
Clause-②: no (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none — no file under `skills/**` teaches SSO domain verification, account linking or an address change through an SSO provider; `content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx` ("Domain verification (opt-in)") states the rule.

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:开启 SSO 域名验证后,"经由身份提供方到达的账号,其邮箱只能位于该提供方已验证的域名"这条规则(此前只管新建账号)现在也管另外两条路径:隐式关联到已有账号,以及会改写已关联账号已存邮箱的登录。会改写邮箱、而新邮箱不在已验证域名时拒绝;无法判定是否会改写时也拒绝;不改写任何东西的登录照常放行。拒绝码为 `EMAIL_DOMAIN_NOT_ALLOWED`,不写关联、不发会话、已存邮箱不变。依据为维护者裁决(review#2 记录 6884303063 转述,选项 B「只拦会改邮箱的登录」)。
- 为什么改:让域名验证的保证在账号被"到达"的每一条会落地变化的路径上都成立,而不只是在新建时;匹配方式与新建时完全相同(精确匹配,子域名须自身列出并验证)。
- 风险与回滚:仅在开启域名验证的环境生效;关闭验证、非 SSO 来源、用户自己发起的显式关联、不改写邮箱的登录(含所有 SAML 提供方,以及平台自身注册流程下从不开启更新的 OIDC 提供方)均不变。本地账号位于"已列出域名的未列出子域名"的人,首次经 SSO 登录会被拒,需把该子域名加到提供方并重新验证;完全未列出的域名此前就不关联,不受影响。回滚即还原本 PR。D6 的 ADR 说明在 #33356(Tier H,另行审批)。
- 先看:`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/implicit-account-linking.ts`(规则 4:`refuseImplicitAccountLink` 新增判定;`refuseSsoAddressChangeOutsideProvenDomain` 与 `ssoSignInWritesAddress`,后者读不到即按"会改写"处理);`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-auth-instance.ts`(`validateUserInfo` 串接顺序);`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-account-at-proven-domain.ts`(仅抽出 `readSsoProviderProvenDomains`,新建规则行为不变)。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth exec vitest run src/implicit-account-linking.test.ts src/sso-oidc-refusal-cause.test.ts src/sso-saml-refusal-landing.test.ts src/sso-account-at-proven-domain.test.ts`,预期 `Tests 255 passed (255)`(合并 main 后)。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地。

## What changes

The rule, as ruled (the maintainer's ruling relayed in review#2 record 6884303063): with SSO domain verification on, an account reached through a provider holds an email address only at a domain that provider has proven. Account creation already follows it. This PR applies the same rule, with the same module, to the two other ways an SSO sign-in (SAML or OIDC) reaches an account:

- **An implicit link.** A sign-in that links to an account that already exists is admitted only when the asserted address is at a domain the provider has proven, compared exactly: a subdomain counts only when it is itself listed and verified (`refuseImplicitAccountLink`, rule 4 in the `implicit-account-linking.ts` header). The two cases are kept apart. An address at a domain the provider does not list at all was already not linked, and is still refused as before with the same answer (pinned as a CONTROL). An address at a subdomain of a listed domain that is not itself listed and verified was linked before and is now refused.
- **A sign-in that would change the stored address.** A sign-in into an already-linked account is refused when it would change the stored address to one outside the proven domains, and refused where whether it would change the address cannot be determined. A sign-in that reports an address outside the proven domains but changes nothing is admitted, as before. This is `refuseSsoAddressChangeOutsideProvenDomain`, chained into `validateUserInfo` after the link gate and before the audience gate. Whether the sign-in writes the address is the vendor's own decision, read from the inputs it reads (`ssoSignInWritesAddress`): for OIDC, the provider's stored update setting, which the platform's own provider registration never turns on; for SAML, none; and a configured `defaultSSO` entry or `resolveUser` selection where one is composed. A decision that cannot be read is judged as a write.
- **The refusal** is `EMAIL_DOMAIN_NOT_ALLOWED`, the code creation answers, with a rule-level description per case that names no domain. No new error code. A provider row that cannot be read refuses; an account that cannot be read throws, which the sign-in answers with the gate's general refusal.
- **Reuse.** The provider read moves out of `refuseSsoAccountOutsideProvenDomain` into the exported `readSsoProviderProvenDomains`. The creation rule's behaviour is unchanged and its tests are untouched.
- **Unchanged.** Verification off; sign-ins that would not change the stored address; non-SSO sources (the cloud identity provider and enterprise OAuth providers); a link the user starts from their own session (an explicit link); the domain-matching rule itself.
- **Texts.** `content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx` states the rule for an implicit link (both cases) and for a sign-in that would change the address. The gate comments in `sso-account-at-proven-domain.ts` and `auth-manager-auth-instance.ts`, the SSO mount comment in `auth-manager-plugin-list.ts`, and the TSDoc of `isSsoDomainVerificationEnabled` all state the rule for creation, implicit link and address change.
- **ADR.** The dated ADR-0135 D6 note recording this extension and its ruling is the separate governed PR #33356.

## Tests

Named by the rule.

- `sso-oidc-refusal-cause.test.ts`, section 6 (real `AuthManager`, real vendor callback, stubbed IdP), covering:
  - an implicit link at an unlisted subdomain: refused, with no `sys_account` row and no session;
  - an implicit link at a domain the provider does not list at all: refused as before (CONTROL);
  - an implicit link at a proven domain: links and signs in;
  - with a provider that updates the account, a change to an outside address or to an unlisted subdomain: refused, stored email unchanged, no new session;
  - a change to another proven domain: applies;
  - with a provider that does not update the account, an outside address asserted later: signs in, and nothing changes;
  - CONTROLS: verification off, and a later sign-in with the stored address.
- `sso-saml-refusal-landing.test.ts`:
  - the implicit-link pair over SAML, plus the verification-off CONTROL;
  - a later SAML sign-in asserting an outside address: signs in, and the stored address is unchanged.
- `implicit-account-linking.test.ts`, new top-level describe: the rule on its own inputs, OIDC and SAML, including:
  - the write decision read as the vendor reads it;
  - fail-closed cases;
  - CONTROLS for verification off, a non-SSO source, an explicit link (an OAuth source), and the creation rule unchanged.
